international.title: Call for police to investigate Scottish hospital after 19 deaths due to surgery
international.summary: Surgeon at Aberdeen Royal Infirmary says he repeatedly voiced concerns that patients may have died unnecessarily A senior surgeon has called for a criminal investigation into a Scottish hospital after it emerged that at least 19 patients had died from avoidable complications due to surgery. Dr Mohammed Habib, a consultant at Aberdeen Royal Infirmary, said he had repeatedly reported concerns about the hospital’s liver and pancreatic surgery from 2021 onwards and believed dozens of patients may have died unnecessarily there.
